lines.text: Toast really does land butter side down.
It is not luck, and it is not Murphy's law.
Watch what actually happens at the edge.
It does not fall flat. It pivots on the edge, and leaves the table already turning.
From a table, it has time for about half a turn.
And half a turn is exactly the wrong number.
Butter side up. A hundred and eighty degrees. Butter side down.
To get all the way round, it would have to fall from about three metres.
So build a three metre table, and the problem goes away.
A table is that height because you are that height.
And how tall a person can be is not a choice either. It is set by how strong chemical bonds are, against gravity.
Fall much further than your own height, and the bonds lose.
Your toast lands butter side down because of the size of atoms.
